templates.promptPattern: The written-out notes in bar {bar} (marked {label}) are the performed version of one ornament on its principal note. Write the ornament that stands for them: a sign above the principal note, or a small note before it for an acciaccatura or appoggiatura.

acceptance.alternativesNote: Accepted alternative signs for the same ornament (e.g. trill symbol variants) are accepted. The reverse task (writing out a sign) is never assessed.

ambiguityChecks: Written-out figure maps to one ornament.
The prompt names the principal note (by label) and says where the ornament goes; the learner never has to guess which note carries it.

Written-out figures use only the standard realisations taught in G5-U5-L01 (for example a turn begins on the note above); a figure that could also be read as another ornament at the same speed is not generated.
An acciaccatura is generated only as a very short note and an appoggiatura only as a note taking about half the principal note's value, so duration, not guesswork, separates them.
hints: Count the written-out notes, then check whether they begin above or below the principal note and whether they return to it.
Decide whether the figure is quick and before the beat (acciaccatura) or takes time from the principal note (appoggiatura).

templates.promptPattern: Which voice type sings this part? The part is described by its written range on a stave or by a typical role; every option set includes the voice types next to the correct one.

acceptance.alternativesNote: One option is correct; distractors are checked to have clearly different meanings.

ambiguityChecks: Distinct ranges.
Range prompts give the actual lowest and highest notes, never only 'highest' or 'lowest', so the answer cannot be found by picking the extreme option.
Options always include the neighbouring voice type(s) (for example alto beside mezzo-soprano, baritone beside tenor and bass) so elimination from the extremes does not work.
Range figures come only from the course's published range table (open question Q15); until a teacher confirms that table, range prompts are not generated and items use role or order comparisons.
hints: Compare the lowest and highest notes of the part with where each voice type usually sits, then choose the voice whose range holds the whole part.

templates.promptPattern: Rewrite this bar of {fromTimeSignature} in {toTimeSignature} so every note and rest keeps the same share of its beat. Beam by the new beats.

acceptance.alternativesNote: One rewrite is correct: each value gains a dot (simple to compound) or loses its dot (compound to simple); beams stay within a beat.

ambiguityChecks: Only regular simple/compound pairs with the same number of beats (2/4–6/8, 3/4–9/8, 4/4–12/8).
Simple to compound uses undotted values only; compound to simple uses fully dotted values only (an undotted compound value would need a triplet, which is outside this exercise).
No ties, tuplets or chords; the prompt states that the beat relationships, not the bar length, are preserved.
hints: Name the beat in each time signature. A crotchet beat becomes a dotted crotchet beat, so each value gains a dot.

extraMistakeCategories.description: Copied the note values into the new time signature unchanged.
extraMistakeCategories.feedback: The beat is a different length in the new time signature. Compare one beat in each: a crotchet beat in 2/4 is a dotted crotchet beat in 6/8, so each value must change with it.

extraMistakeCategories.description: Rewrote the notes but left a rest unchanged.
extraMistakeCategories.feedback: Rests follow the same rule as notes: they fill the same share of the beat, so they need the same change.

extraMistakeCategories.description: Kept the dots when rewriting from compound to simple time.
extraMistakeCategories.feedback: A simple beat is undotted (a crotchet or minim), so the dot that made each compound beat disappears.

extraMistakeCategories.description: Beamed notes from different beats together.
extraMistakeCategories.feedback: Keep each beat's notes together and start a new beam on each new beat, so the beats can be seen.
